claim: The contractile ring is a complex molecular apparatus which physically divides many eukaryotic cells.
source: The contractile ring is a complex molecular apparatus which physically divides many eukaryotic cells.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the contractile ring's function in cell division.

claim: Proteins in the contractile ring localize in specific layers relative to the membrane.
source: Similar to other membrane-tethered actin structures, we find proteins localize in specific layers relative to the membrane.
evidence: This claim is supported by the fPALM experimental data presented in the manuscript showing distinct protein localizations at different distances from the membrane.

claim: The most membrane-proximal layer (0–80 nm) is composed of membrane-binding scaffolds, formin, and the tail of the essential myosin-II.
source: The most membrane-proximal layer (0–80 nm) is composed of membrane-binding scaffolds, formin, and the tail of the essential myosin-II.
evidence: This claim is directly supported by fPALM measurements showing the spatial distribution of these proteins relative to the membrane.

claim: An intermediate layer (80–160 nm) consists of a network of cytokinesis accessory proteins as well as multiple signaling components which influence cell division.
source: An intermediate layer (80–160 nm) consists of a network of cytokinesis accessory proteins as well as multiple signaling components which influence cell division.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM data showing the localization of accessory proteins and signaling components at this distance from the membrane.

claim: Farthest from the membrane (160–350 nm) are F-actin, the motor domains of myosins, and a major F-actin crosslinker.
source: Farthest from the membrane (160–350 nm) we find F-actin, the motor domains of myosins, and a major F-actin crosslinker.
evidence: This claim is supported by fPALM measurements of F-actin, myosin motor domains, and Fim1 localization.

claim: Multiple proteins proximal to the membrane form clusters of different sizes.
source: Circumferentially within the ring, multiple proteins proximal to the membrane form clusters of different sizes, while components farther from the membrane are uniformly distributed.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging and IDM analysis showing clustering patterns for membrane-proximal proteins.

claim: Components farther from the membrane are uniformly distributed.
source: Circumferentially within the ring, multiple proteins proximal to the membrane form clusters of different sizes, while components farther from the membrane are uniformly distributed.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging showing uniform distribution of F-actin and distal protein domains.

claim: The contractile ring uses myosin motors to constrict an F-actin ring.
source: This complex structure is tightly linked to the plasma membrane and uses myosin motors to constrict an F-actin ring (Cheffings et al., 2016), pulling opposing sides of the membrane together.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on contractile ring mechanics.

claim: 318 proteins are annotated as localizing to the S. pombe division site.
source: 318 proteins are annotated as localizing to the S. pombe division site (Matsuyama et al., 2006; Wood et al., 2012), which includes both the contractile ring and the lining of the division septum formed during ring constriction.
evidence: This is supported by citations to genome-wide localization studies.

claim: Only 38 proteins make up the contractile ring itself according to PomBase annotation.
source: Only a subset of these proteins (38 according to PomBase annotation [Wood et al., 2012]) make up the contractile ring itself.
evidence: This is supported by citation to the PomBase database annotation.

claim: The S. pombe contractile ring forms in the middle of the cell from precursor 'nodes'.
source: The S. pombe contractile ring forms in the middle of the cell from precursor 'nodes', membrane-tethered protein foci that contain anillin Mid1, IQGAP Rng2, myosin-II heavy chain Myo2 and light chains Cdc4 and Rlc1, F-BAR Cdc15, and formin Cdc12 (Wu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on contractile ring assembly.

claim: Precursor nodes coalesce into a contiguous ring over ~20 min.
source: Precursor nodes coalesce into a contiguous ring over ~20 min that recruits many additional components over a further ~20 min before constriction after mitotic exit.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on ring assembly kinetics.

claim: The contractile ring is only 100–200 nm in width.
source: Ultimately, the resolution limit of conventional fluorescence microscopy (~250 nm) restrains the spatial information attainable by studies of S. pombe nodes and contractile rings, each only 100–200 nm in width (Wu et al., 2006; Laplante et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior measurements of contractile ring dimensions.

claim: The ring is composed of a dense array of 1000–2000 F-actin filaments with mixed directionality.
source: At higher resolution, one electron microscopy study revealed that the ring is composed of a dense array of 1000–2000 F-actin filaments with mixed directionality (Kamasaki et al., 2007); however, additional protein components could not be detected with this technique.
evidence: This is supported by citation to an electron microscopy study.

claim: In focal adhesions, the plasma membrane and F-actin are separated by distinct layers of proteins.
source: In focal adhesions, the plasma membrane and F-actin were found to be separated by distinct layers of proteins: an integrin signaling layer, a force transduction layer, and an actin regulatory layer (Kanchanawong et al., 2010), revealing a potential mechanism of force-induced focal adhesion formation and maintenance.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior super-resolution work on focal adhesions.

claim: mMaple3 has a faster maturation time (49 min) than mEos3.2 (330 min).
source: The photoactivatable mMaple3 fluorophore was chosen because it has multiple advantages over the commonly used mEos3.2 (Zhang et al., 2012), most importantly a faster maturation time (49 versus 330 min) (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the literature on fluorophore properties.

claim: The mMaple3 fluorophore is ~5 nm in size.
source: The mMaple3 fluorophore is ~5 nm in size and was connected to protein termini with a short 11 amino acid linker, minimizing positional uncertainty.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of fluorescent protein dimensions.

claim: An average of 34 and 37 nm localization uncertainty was achieved for mMaple3 and ATTO647N fluorophores, respectively.
source: Overall, we achieved an average of 34 and 37 nm localization uncertainty for mMaple3 and ATTO647N fluorophores, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is directly measured from the fPALM data as shown in Figure 1D.

claim: mCling-ATTO647N colocalizes with the FM4-64 membrane dye.
source: First, we verified that mCling-ATTO647N colocalizes with the FM4-64 membrane dye (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental imaging data showing colocalization.

claim: The interior edge of the mCling signal aligns extremely well with the edge of an Acyl-mMaple3 signal.
source: Nevertheless, the interior edge of the mCling signal aligns extremely well with the edge of an Acyl-mMaple3 signal, validating the use of mCling to mark the cytosolic face of the plasma membrane (blue line, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by super-resolution imaging data comparing the two membrane markers.

claim: The fully-formed contractile ring is made up of components 182 ± 26 nm wide.
source: Overall, we found the fully-formed contractile ring is made up of components 182 ± 26 nm wide and extends from the plasma membrane 293 ± 64 nm into the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is calculated from the fPALM measurements of all structural components.

claim: The contractile ring extends from the plasma membrane 293 ± 64 nm into the cytoplasm.
source: Overall, we found the fully-formed contractile ring is made up of components 182 ± 26 nm wide and extends from the plasma membrane 293 ± 64 nm into the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is calculated from the fPALM measurements showing the maximum distance of components from the membrane.

claim: Multiple membrane-binding proteins including anillin Mid1, F-BAR proteins Cdc15 and Imp2, and septin Spn3 are positioned within 80 nm of the plasma membrane.
source: Multiple membrane-binding proteins including the anillin Mid1, the F-BAR proteins Cdc15 and Imp2, and the septin Spn3 are positioned within 80 nm of the plasma membrane.
evidence: This is directly measured by fPALM analysis of these proteins' distances from the membrane.

claim: Both termini of Mid1 are within 50 nm of the membrane.
source: Both termini of Mid1 are within 50 nm of the membrane, consistent with direct membrane binding through its C2 domain (Sun et al., 2015; Rincon and Paoletti, 2012; Celton-Morizur et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Mid1's membrane binding.

claim: Cdc15 and Imp2 contain N-terminal F-BAR domains that directly bind the membrane.
source: Cdc15 and Imp2 contain N-terminal F-BAR domains that also directly bind the membrane (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2010; McDonald et al., 2016; McDonald et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on F-BAR domain membrane binding.

claim: The C-terminal tail of the essential contractile ring myosin-II Myo2 is near the membrane.
source: In addition to membrane-binding proteins, the C-terminal tail of the essential contractile ring myosin-II Myo2 (Kitayama et al., 1997; Palani et al., 2017) is near the membrane, as was observed in cytokinesis precursor nodes (Laporte et al., 2011; Laplante et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Myo2 localization.

claim: The N-terminus of the formin Cdc12 is found near the membrane.
source: The N-terminus of the formin Cdc12 is also found near the membrane, in accord with direct binding to the F-BAR domain of Cdc15 (Willet et al., 2015b; Carnahan and Gould, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Cdc12-Cdc15 interaction.

claim: IQGAP Rng2 is found 80–160 nm from the membrane.
source: Slightly further from the membrane (80–160 nm) we find the IQGAP Rng2, a scaffolding protein critical for contractile ring formation and constriction (Padmanabhan et al., 2011; Tebbs and Pollard, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Rng2 function.

claim: Multiple accessory proteins important for ring integrity are present in the 80-160 nm layer: Cyk3, Spa2, Blt1, paxillin Pxl1, Nod1, and Fic1.
source: Multiple accessory proteins important for ring integrity are also present in this layer and are linked to the underlying layer through direct protein-protein interactions: Cyk3, Spa2, Blt1, paxillin Pxl1, Nod1, and Fic1 (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2010; Bohnert and Gould, 2012; Ren et al., 2015; Pollard et al., 2012; Zhu et al., 2013; Guzman-Vendrell et al., 2013; Pinar et al., 2008; Ge and Balasubramanian, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on these proteins.

claim: The tail domains of myosin-II Myp2 and myosin-V Myo51 are found at intermediate distances from the membrane.
source: At similar intermediate distances from the membrane, we find the tail domains of two additional myosins that contribute to S. pombe cytokinesis: the non-essential myosin-II, Myp2 (Bezanilla et al., 1997; Mulvihill and Hyams, 2003), as well as a myosin-V, Myo51 (Win et al., 2001; Tang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on these myosins.

claim: The C-termini of three F-BAR proteins (Cdc15, Imp2, and Rga7) extend away from their membrane-bound F-BAR domains into the intermediate layer of the ring.
source: Interestingly, we find that the C-termini of three F-BAR proteins (Cdc15, Imp2, and Rga7) extend away from their membrane-bound F-BAR domains into the intermediate layer of the ring (lines, Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements of both termini of these proteins showing spatial separation.

claim: F-BAR proteins contain central regions predicted to be unstructured, which may permit the SH3 domains to extend inward ~100 nm distances.
source: These proteins contain central regions predicted to be unstructured, which may permit the SH3 domains of Cdc15 and Imp2 to extend inward ~100 nm distances and connect with their multiple interactors also found at this layer including Pxl1, Spa2, Fic1, Cyk3 (Figure 2), and Rgf3 (Figure 3) (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2010; Ren et al., 2015; Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on inference from structural predictions and fPALM data showing the spatial separation of F-BAR and SH3 domains.

claim: F-actin is found at the farthest distances from the membrane (160–350 nm).
source: At the farthest distances from the membrane (160–350 nm), we find F-actin, the motor domains of the type II and type V myosins Myo2, Myp2, and Myo51, as well as Fim1, an F-actin crosslinker (Figure 2).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements using LifeAct-mMaple3 and Phalloidin-Alexa488.

claim: F-actin's dcenter is at 219 ± 64 nm (LifeAct-mMaple3) or 228 ± 75 nm (Phalloidin) from the membrane.
source: Measurements using these two methods were consistent, placing F-actin's dcenter at 219 ± 64 (LifeAct-mMaple3) or 228 ± 75 nm (Phalloidin; Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) from the membrane.
evidence: This is directly measured by fPALM analysis using two different F-actin probes.

claim: The N-terminal head domains of Myo2, Myp2, and Myo51 are level with F-actin.
source: The N-terminal head domains of Myo2, Myp2, and Myo51 are level with F-actin, while the light chain Rlc1 is ~30 nm closer to the membrane, in accord with its binding to the neck domains of myosin motors that are immediately proximal to the head domains (Naqvi et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on myosin structure.

claim: The kinases Orb2/Pak1/Shk1, Sid2, and Pck1 are relatively close to the membrane, on average <110 nm.
source: The kinases Orb2/Pak1/Shk1, Sid2, and Pck1 are relatively close to the membrane, on average <110 nm.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements of these signaling proteins.

claim: The N-terminus of the kinase Pom1 was found farther away from the membrane (149 nm) despite the presence of a nearby membrane-binding motif.
source: In contrast, the N-terminus of the kinase Pom1 was found farther away from the membrane (149 nm) despite the presence of a nearby membrane-binding motif (Hachet et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citation to prior work on Pom1's membrane binding.

claim: The RhoGEF Rgf3 is present at an intermediate height.
source: The RhoGEF Rgf3, a known partner of Cdc15 and Imp2 SH3 domains (Ren et al., 2015), is also present at an intermediate height.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citation to prior work on Rgf3 interactions.

claim: Phosphatases Clp1 and Ppb1, RhoGAP Rga2, and RhoGEF Gef2 were found in an intermediate stratum.
source: Phosphatases Clp1 (Cdc14-related) and Ppb1 (Calcineurin), RhoGAP Rga2, and RhoGEF Gef2 were also found in an intermediate stratum.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements of these signaling proteins.

claim: Gef2 is in complex with Nod1 and is found at a similar elevation to its binding partner, 145 nm and 140 nm, respectively.
source: Gef2 is in complex with Nod1 (Zhu et al., 2013) and is found at a similar elevation to its binding partner, 145 nm and 140 nm, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citation to prior work on Gef2-Nod1 interaction.

claim: The majority of Rad24 is found high in elevation, similar to F-actin, though it also localizes throughout the cytoplasm.
source: We find the majority of Rad24 high in elevation, similar to F-actin, though it also localizes throughout the cytoplasm.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements showing Rad24's spatial distribution.

claim: Combining tagged proteins from adjacent layers results in a single peak that is significantly wider.
source: Next, we combined tagged proteins from adjacent layers: mMaple3-Cdc15 and Imp2-mMaple3, as well as mMaple3-Cdc15-mMaple3 with tags on its two termini in proximal and intermediate layers. In these cases, a single peak was still observed, but the peak was significantly wider, matching predictions (green dashed lines, Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements of dual-tagged strains showing increased peak width.

claim: Combining proteins in proximal and distal layers results in either an even wider peak or two resolvable peaks.
source: Finally, we examined strains containing proteins in proximal and distal layers: mMaple3-Cdc15 and mMaple3-Myo2, along with mMaple3-Cdc15 and LifeAct-mMaple3. In these cases, either an even wider peak or two resolvable peaks were observed, confirming the spatial separation of proximal and distal components (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements of dual-tagged strains showing spatial separation.

claim: FRET was detected between mCherry-Cdc15 and membrane-bound Acyl-GFP.
source: Supporting the hypothesis that Cdc15 and probably other F-BARs scaffold distinct layers of proteins in the contractile ring, we detected specific FRET signals between mCherry-Cdc15 and membrane-bound Acyl-GFP, GFP-Imp2, GFP-Rga7, and both mNG-Cdc12 and Cdc12-mNG (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by FRET measurements showing energy transfer between these proteins.

claim: A strong FRET signal between mCherry-Cdc15 and Acyl-GFP is consistent with the binding of Cdc15's F-BAR to anionic phospholipids within the plasma membrane.
source: A strong FRET signal between mCherry-Cdc15 and Acyl-GFP is consistent with the binding of Cdc15's F-BAR to anionic phospholipids within the plasma membrane (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2010; McDonald et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data and citations to prior work on Cdc15 membrane binding.

claim: The FRET signal of mCherry-Cdc15 with two other F-BAR domains (GFP-Imp2 and GFP-Rga7) indicates that all three cytokinesis F-BARs are packed in close proximity upon the membrane.
source: Furthermore, the FRET signal of mCherry-Cdc15 with two other F-BAR domains (GFP-Imp2 and GFP-Rga7) indicates that all three cytokinesis F-BARs are packed in close proximity upon the membrane, despite the fact that they do not heterodimerize (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2009; Martín-García et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by FRET data and citations to prior work showing F-BARs do not heterodimerize.

claim: Cdc15-mCherry showed significant FRET signals with Imp2-GFP, Rga7-GFP, and five known binding partners of its SH3 domain: Fic1-GFP, Pxl1-GFP, GFP-Spa2, GFP-Rgf3, and GFP-Cyk3.
source: Cdc15-mCherry, on the other hand, showed significant FRET signals with Imp2-GFP, Rga7-GFP, and five known binding partners of its SH3 domain: Fic1-GFP, Pxl1-GFP, GFP-Spa2, GFP-Rgf3, and GFP-Cyk3 (Figure 5B) (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2010; Ren et al., 2015; Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by FRET measurements and citations to prior work on SH3 domain interactions.

claim: The specificity of the FRET signal for Cdc15-mCherry over mCherry-Cdc15 supports the extended orientation of Cdc15 proposed from fPALM analysis.
source: Moreover, the specificity of the signal for Cdc15-mCherry over mCherry-Cdc15 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B) supports the extended orientation of Cdc15 proposed from our fPALM analysis.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of FRET signals between different Cdc15 tag orientations.

claim: F-actin, detected by LifeAct-mMaple3, was distributed uniformly along the ring circumference.
source: Distally, F-actin, detected by LifeAct-mMaple3, was distributed uniformly along the ring circumference, consistent with electron micrographs of the ring (Kamasaki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging and IDM analysis, and citation to electron microscopy.

claim: The N-terminus of Myo2 was uniformly distributed.
source: Also in the distal layer, the N-terminus of Myo2 was uniformly distributed.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging and IDM analysis.

claim: The C-termini of Myp2, Fic1, and Cdc15 were evenly distributed.
source: Within the intermediate layer, the C-termini of Myp2, Fic1, and Cdc15 were evenly distributed.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging and IDM analysis.

claim: The domains of Cdc15 and Myo2 close to the membrane appeared to form clusters spaced at regular intervals along the circumferential axis with diameters of 71 ± 17 and 104 ± 26 nm, respectively.
source: In contrast, the domains of Cdc15 and Myo2 close to the membrane appeared to form clusters spaced at regular intervals along the circumferential axis with diameters of 71 ± 17 and 104 ± 26 nm, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging showing clustering patterns.

claim: Rng2 and Mid1 were present in larger, unevenly spaced clusters 201 ± 49 and 200 ± 44 nm in diameter, respectively.
source: Also in the proximal layer, Rng2 and Mid1 were present in larger, unevenly spaced clusters 201 ± 49 and 200 ± 44 nm in diameter, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging showing clustering patterns.

claim: Spn3 displayed a uniform distribution.
source: Though these clustered components all reside in the proximal layer, not all proximal components were clustered. Spn3 displayed a uniform distribution which might be expected for dense septin filament bundles that are not entirely in register (Oh and Bi, 2011) and because septins are never present in early cytokinesis nodes (Tasto et al., 2003; Berlin et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM imaging and citations to prior work on septin organization.

claim: A mMaple3-Cdc15(E30K E152K) oligomerization mutant prevented cluster formation.
source: Cdc15's N-terminal F-BAR forms linear oligomers (McDonald et al., 2015); to test if oligomerization was responsible for organization of the observed larger scale clusters, we imaged a mMaple3-Cdc15(E30K E152K) oligomerization mutant. Indeed the oligomerization mutant prevented cluster formation.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM imaging of the oligomerization mutant and citation to prior work on Cdc15 oligomerization.

claim: The oligomerization mutation resulted in a widened mMaple3-Cdc15 ring thickness.
source: Interestingly, the oligomerization mutation also resulted in a widened mMaple3-Cdc15 ring thickness, suggesting oligomerization may also help concentrate Cdc15 in the ring.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements of the oligomerization mutant showing increased ring width.

claim: The deletion of mid1 did not prevent Cdc15 cluster formation.
source: In contrast, the deletion of mid1 did not prevent Cdc15 cluster formation.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM imaging of mid1Δ cells showing persistent Cdc15 clustering.

claim: The contractile ring is composed of distinct connected layers rising from the plasma membrane and extending up to 350 nm towards the interior of the cell.
source: Using fPALM super-resolution imaging, we have determined the spatial organization of 29 central components of the contractile ring relative to the membrane. We found that these components organize into distinct connected layers rising from the plasma membrane and extending up to 350 nm towards the interior of the cell (Figure 7 and Video 1).
evidence: This is a summary of the fPALM data showing the layered organization of the contractile ring.

claim: The contractile ring's layered organization is similar to focal adhesions and cadherin junctions.
source: Our analysis of 29 components of the contractile ring by fPALM indicates the existence of distinct layers tethering F-actin to the plasma membrane, similar to two previously investigated membrane-tethered F-actin structures, focal adhesions (Kanchanawong et al., 2010) and cadherin junctions (Bertocchi et al., 2017).
evidence: This is based on comparison of the contractile ring architecture to prior super-resolution studies of other structures.

claim: The anillin Mid1, tethered to the membrane via its C2 domain, binds the tail of the essential type II myosin, Myo2.
source: The anillin Mid1, tethered to the membrane via its C2 domain, binds the tail of the essential type II myosin, Myo2 (Motegi et al., 2004), as well as extending to bind IQGAP Rng2 (Padmanabhan et al., 2011), which in turn stabilizes the Myo2-Mid1 interaction (Laporte et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on Mid1 interactions.

claim: The F-BAR domain of Cdc15 scaffolds the formin Cdc12.
source: The F-BAR domain of Cdc15, also bound directly to the membrane, scaffolds the formin Cdc12 (Willet et al., 2015b; Carnahan and Gould, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on Cdc15-Cdc12 interaction.

claim: Additional time is required to assemble the ring when Mid1 is missing.
source: In fact, additional time is required to assemble the ring when Mid1 is missing (Huang et al., 2008b; Hachet and Simanis, 2008; Wu et al., 2003), while rings can slide and disassemble when Cdc15 abundance is reduced (McDonald et al., 2015; Arasada and Pollard, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on Mid1 and Cdc15 function.

claim: The ring remains associated with the plasma membrane in the majority of cells lacking Mid1 or fully functional Cdc15 or both.
source: It is surprising that the ring remains associated with the plasma membrane in the majority of cells lacking Mid1 or fully functional Cdc15 or both (McDonald et al., 2015), indicating that other ring components important for establishing this tight plasma membrane-contractile ring linkage must exist, especially during constriction when Mid1 leaves the ring (Wu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on ring stability in mutants.

claim: The SH3 domains of Cdc15 and Imp2 are functionally redundant.
source: At 80–160 nm away from the membrane, we find the C-termini of Cdc15 and Imp2, which contain their SH3 domains. These domains are functionally redundant (Ren et al., 2015), but having one or the other is essential for cytokinesis and cell viability (Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2009), demonstrating the importance of an SH3-scaffolded network within the contractile ring.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on SH3 domain function.

claim: Synthetic lethality has been observed when null alleles of intermediate layer genes were combined.
source: In support of this hypothesis, synthetic lethality has been observed in several cases when null alleles of these genes were combined (Ren et al., 2015; Pinar et al., 2008; Roberts-Galbraith et al., 2009; Liu et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior genetic studies.

claim: In the complete absence of Cdc15 and its SH3 interaction network, F-actin rings can still form but quickly disintegrate.
source: Indeed in the complete absence of Cdc15 and its SH3 interaction network, F-actin rings can still form but quickly disintegrate (Laporte et al., 2011), underscoring the stabilizing function of the intermediate zone.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on Cdc15 function.

claim: The elevated localization and ~200 nm thickness of F-actin matches the limited electron micrographs of S. pombe rings that are available.
source: Farthest from the membrane (160–350 nm), we find the center of F-actin localization. The elevated localization and ~200 nm thickness of F-actin matches the limited electron micrographs of S. pombe rings that are available (Kamasaki et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of fPALM data to prior electron microscopy studies.

claim: Classical electron microscopy studies of animal cells have measured the contractile ring as 250–500 nm thick vertically from the membrane.
source: It is notable that classical electron microscopy studies of animal cells have also measured the contractile ring as 250–500 nm thick vertically from the membrane (Schroeder, 1973).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior electron microscopy work on animal cell contractile rings.

claim: Both termini of the formin Cdc12 are significantly closer to the membrane than F-actin.
source: Interestingly, both termini of the formin Cdc12, which nucleates and elongates F-actin in the ring de novo, are significantly closer to the membrane.
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements showing Cdc12 localization relative to F-actin.

claim: F-actin may be nucleated and polymerized by Cdc12 close to the membrane, but filaments are pulled upward and incorporated into the main F-actin density by tension from myosin motors and actin crosslinkers.
source: This localization suggests that F-actin may be nucleated and polymerized by Cdc12 close to the membrane, but filaments are pulled upward and incorporated into the main F-actin density by tension from myosin motors and actin crosslinkers.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial organization of Cdc12, F-actin, myosins, and crosslinkers.

claim: The essential myosin-II Myo2 is oriented with its tail close to the membrane and motor extended, an orientation also seen in precursor nodes.
source: Indeed we found the head domains of all 3 contractile ring myosins and the actin crosslinker Fim1 at a high elevation apposed to F-actin. The essential myosin-II Myo2 is oriented with its tail close to the membrane and motor extended, an orientation also seen in precursor nodes (Laporte et al., 2011; Laplante et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Myo2 orientation.

claim: Myo2's orientation implies a different organization than the canonical bipolar filaments that are observed in sarcomeres and mammalian cleavage furrows.
source: This implies a different organization than the canonical bipolar filaments that are observed in sarcomeres and mammalian cleavage furrows (Fenix et al., 2016; Henson et al., 2017; Pollard et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the Myo2 orientation data and citations to prior work on myosin organization in other systems.

claim: Myo2 has been implicated in ring formation independent of its motor activity.
source: Myo2 has additionally been implicated in ring formation independent of its motor activity (Palani et al., 2017), a function that may be contained within domains near the membrane and other early ring components.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on Myo2 function and inference about domain localization.

claim: Myp2 and Myo51 are single-headed myosin motors.
source: We find the tails of the non-essential myosins Myp2 and Myo51 at an intermediate layer. Myp2 and Myo51 are single-headed myosin motors (Tang et al., 2016; Bezanilla and Pollard, 2000); embedding their tail domains in the intermediate layer may also aid in force generation upon the distal F-actin.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on myosin structure.

claim: Relative to the membrane, ring components tended to organize into similarly 'thick' strata of ~150–200 nm.
source: Relative to the membrane, ring components tended to organize into similarly 'thick' strata of ~150–200 nm.
evidence: This is calculated from the σvert parameters measured by fPALM.

claim: In terms of width within the ring, components organized in widths between 120–220 nm.
source: In terms of width within the ring, components organized in widths between 120–220 nm, with Fim1-mMaple3 being widest and mMaple3-Imp2 being thinnest, though in general widths did not significantly correlate with components' distance from the membrane.
evidence: This is calculated from the σwidth parameters measured by fPALM.

claim: The protein kinase Sid2 is localized at a low elevation (88 nm), properly placed to access its substrates Cdc12, Spa2, and Clp1.
source: We did find that most localized in the correct areas for modification of their reported substrates. Sid2 is localized at a low elevation (88 nm), properly placed to access its substrates Cdc12 (Bohnert et al., 2013), Spa2 (Gupta et al., 2013), and Clp1 (Chen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Sid2 substrates.

claim: The protein kinase Pom1 is in the intermediate layer (175 nm), overlapping with the localization of 3 known substrates: Imp2, Cdc15, and Rga7.
source: The protein kinase Pom1 is in the intermediate layer (175 nm), overlapping with the localization of 3 known substrates: Imp2, Cdc15, and Rga7 (Kettenbach et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citation to prior work on Pom1 substrates.

claim: The Clp1 phosphatase is present at a low-to-intermediate level (136 nm), near its scaffold Mid1 and known and predicted ring substrates.
source: Furthermore, the Clp1 phosphatase is present at a low-to-intermediate level (136 nm), near its scaffold Mid1 (Clifford et al., 2008) and known and predicted ring substrates Cdc15, Blt1, Rng2, Cyk3, Myp2, and Orb2 (Clifford et al., 2008; Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on Clp1 substrates.

claim: Mid1 and Rng2 form irregularly spaced 200 nm clusters, which resemble the size and shape of cytokinesis precursor nodes.
source: Mid1 and Rng2 form irregularly spaced 200 nm clusters, which resemble the size and shape of cytokinesis precursor nodes previously measured with different techniques (conventional microscopy and live cell fPALM) (Wu et al., 2006; Laporte et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM measurements and citations to prior work on node dimensions.

claim: The membrane-proximal termini of Myo2 and Cdc15 form smaller 70–100 nm diameter regularly-spaced clusters along the circumference of the ring.
source: The membrane-proximal termini of Myo2 and Cdc15 form smaller 70–100 nm diameter regularly-spaced clusters along the circumference of the ring.
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM measurements showing clustering patterns.

claim: The very different diameter and regularity of Cdc15 and Myo2 clusters from those of Mid1 and Rng2 argues that node structures change as the ring develops.
source: However, the very different diameter and regularity of Cdc15 and Myo2 clusters from those of Mid1 and Rng2 argues that at the least, node structures change as the ring develops.
evidence: This is inferred from the differences in clustering patterns observed by fPALM.

claim: Mid1 dissociates from the ring as it constricts.
source: This is perhaps to be expected since Mid1, responsible for setting up precursor nodes, dissociates from the ring as it constricts (Wu and Pollard, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on Mid1 dynamics.

claim: Myo2 is concentrated during constriction while Cdc15, Rng2, and Cdc12 remain at a constant concentration.
source: Additionally, the relative stoichiometry of certain components in the ring change during constriction: Myo2 is concentrated during constriction while Cdc15, Rng2, and Cdc12 remain at a constant concentration (Wu and Pollard, 2005; Wu et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior quantitative studies of protein dynamics.

claim: The F-actin signal from LifeAct-mMaple3 is uniform, in accord with electron microscopy studies of contractile ring F-actin.
source: Interestingly, we found components that are further away from the membrane are uniform in their distribution, even compared to their opposite termini. In particular, the F-actin signal from LifeAct-mMaple3 is uniform, in accord with electron microscopy studies of contractile ring F-actin which show a relatively even distribution in both S. pombe and animal cells (Kamasaki et al., 2007; Henson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by circumferential fPALM measurements and citations to electron microscopy studies.

claim: The even distribution of Myo2's head domain is in contrast to myosin-II 'stacks' formed in animal cells.
source: The even distribution of Myo2's head domain suggests a generally even binding of actin throughout the ring. This distribution is in contrast to myosin-II 'stacks' formed in animal cells, where antiparallel myosin units are assembled into large-scale clusters parallel to F-actin filaments (Fenix et al., 2016; Henson et al., 2017).
evidence: This is inferred from the fPALM data and citations to prior work on animal cell myosin organization.

claim: The different layers seen in the fPALM analysis generally correlate with the order of assembly of their components.
source: Together with prior knowledge of when proteins are recruited to the ring, the spatial architecture of the contractile ring determined here suggests possible mechanics of ring formation. In fact, the different layers seen in our analysis generally correlate with the order of assembly of their components.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the fPALM spatial data with prior knowledge of assembly order.

claim: Of the earliest ring components which are recruited to precursor nodes, 4/5 contain termini present within the proximal membrane layer (0–80 nm).
source: Of the earliest ring components which are recruited to precursor nodes (Mid1, Rng2, Myo2, Cdc15, and Cdc12) (Wu et al., 2006; Laporte et al., 2011), 4/5 contain termini present within the proximal membrane layer (0–80 nm), and 2/5 contain direct membrane binding domains.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the fPALM data in relation to prior knowledge of node composition.

claim: The precise order of assembly of Rng2, Myo2, and Cdc12 does not appear to matter for ring formation.
source: The precise order of assembly of Rng2, Myo2, and Cdc12 does not appear to matter for ring formation (Tao et al., 2014), but it seems likely that the initial setup of the ring involves the construction of a membrane-anchored scaffold.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work on assembly order and inference about scaffold formation.

claim: F-actin is formed de novo at nodes and the ring by Cdc12 as well as incorporated from longitudinal actin cables.
source: F-actin is formed de novo at nodes and the ring by Cdc12 (Pelham and Chang, 2002) as well as incorporated from longitudinal actin cables (Huang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on F-actin assembly mechanisms.

claim: F-actin may be principally held in its elevated location by the tension from the motor activity of myosins.
source: F-actin, though turning over quickly in the ring (Henson et al., 2017), may be principally held in its elevated location by the tension from the motor activity of myosins.
evidence: This is inferred from the spatial organization and citations to prior work on F-actin dynamics.

claim: Components that join the ring later are generally present within the intermediate layer.
source: Once a contiguous ring is formed, many additional components are recruited. Components that join the ring later are generally present within the intermediate layer.
evidence: This is inferred from comparing the fPALM spatial data with prior knowledge of assembly timing.
